questions.question: Day 13 Practice (Travel, Autos & Cabs (Phase 2)): When talking about rescheduling a team sync (by 5:00 PM), which sentence is grammatically correct for 'My colleague'?

options.a: I am rescheduling a team sync right now.
options.b: Could we reschedule our sync meeting to 3:00 PM?
options.c: Shift meeting 3 clock possible?
options.d: Shift meeting 3 clock possible? yesterday

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
Natural everyday English uses standard tense agreement: "Could we reschedule our sync meeting to 3:00 PM?".

questions.question: Day 13 Vocabulary (Travel, Autos & Cabs (Phase 2)): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'touch base'?

options.a: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.
options.b: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.
options.c: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.
options.d: Briefly connect with someone to exchange news.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
'touch base' means: briefly connect with someone to exchange news. Example: "I will touch base with you after the review."

questions.question: Day 13 Vocabulary (Travel, Autos & Cabs (Phase 2)): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'freshen up'?

options.a: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.
options.b: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.
options.c: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.
options.d: Wash hands and face to relax after travel.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
'freshen up' means: wash hands and face to relax after travel. Example: "Let me freshen up after returning home."

questions.question: Day 13 Terms (Travel, Autos & Cabs (Phase 2)): Choose the correct definition for the phrasal verb 'drop by':

options.a: Visit someone informally for a short time.
options.b: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.
options.c: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.
options.d: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option A
'drop by' means: visit someone informally for a short time. Example: "Feel free to drop by our home this evening."

questions.question: Day 13 Terms (Travel, Autos & Cabs (Phase 2)): Choose the correct definition for the phrasal verb 'drop off':

options.a: Take someone to a destination and leave them there.
options.b: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.
options.c: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.
options.d: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option A
'drop off' means: take someone to a destination and leave them there. Example: "Please drop me off near the bus stand."

questions.question:
Day 13 Translation Scenario 1 (Travel, Autos & Cabs (Phase 2)):

Telugu: "నా పార్సెల్ ఈ రోజు సాయంత్రానికి డెలివరీ అవుతుందా?"
(Literal attempt: "My parcel today evening delivery becoming?")

options.a: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.b: I am needing to my parcel today evening delivery becoming?
options.c: My parcel today evening delivery becoming?
options.d: Will my package be delivered by this evening?

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
Natural Version: "Will my package be delivered by this evening?"

Use 'Will my package be delivered...' for delivery tracking.

questions.question:
Day 13 Translation Scenario 2 (Travel, Autos & Cabs (Phase 2)):

Telugu: "ఈ టమాటాలు కేజీ ఎంత? కొంచెం తాజావి ఏరి ఇవ్వండి."
(Literal attempt: "These tomatoes kg how much? Pick give fresh.")

options.a: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.b: These tomatoes kg how much? Pick give fresh.
options.c: How much are these tomatoes per kilo? Please pick out fresh ones for me.
options.d: I am needing to these tomatoes kg how much? pick give fresh.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option C
Natural Version: "How much are these tomatoes per kilo? Please pick out fresh ones for me."

Use 'per kilo' for price and 'pick out' for selection.

questions.question:
Day 13 Translation Scenario 3 (Travel, Autos & Cabs (Phase 2)):

(Literal attempt: "Evening my house come, tea drink.")

options.a: Evening my house come, tea drink.
options.b: I am needing to evening my house come, tea drink.
options.c: Please drop by our home this evening; we can have tea together.
options.d: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option C
Natural Version: "Please drop by our home this evening; we can have tea together."

Use 'drop by our home' for informal invitations.
